description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/universal.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  4 blessed rows, three separate shapes of
`can` that the round measured but did not fix.

(a) `->can` FOR A FORWARD-DECLARED SUB (t/op/universal.t line 78, test 18)

      sub Alice::sing;                 # declared, no body
      ok $ref = $a->can("sing");       # perl: a CODE ref.  PCL: false

    perl's `can` answers the stash slot's CV, which a forward declaration
    creates (and calling it then dies "Undefined subroutine", which is what
    the next two rows of the file assert).  PCL has no slot for a body-less
    declaration, so `can` says no.  Same family as #1664, the typeglob /
    stash-slot model.

(b) A CLASS NAME THAT IS A NUMBER (line 111, test 75; and test 77)

      ok UNIVERSAL::can(23, "can");     # perl 1     PCL false
      ++${"23::foo"};                   # vivifies the stash
      ok UNIVERSAL::can("23", "can"), '"23" can can when the pack exists';
      ok UNIVERSAL::can(23, "can"),   '23 can can when the pack exists';

    Test 76 (the STRING spelling) PASSES and test 77 (the NUMBER spelling)
    does not, so the divergence is in how the invocant is coerced to a class
    name, not in `can` itself.  #1650 taught the compiler perl's all-digit
    NAME rule for containers; this is the same question for a class.

(c) `can` ON AN IO BAREWORD (test 80, `IO barewords can`)

    A filehandle used as an invocant must find UNIVERSAL's methods.  Adjacent
    to #1453 (`*FH{IO}` yields the GLOB, not an IO::File object).

Rows: t/op/universal.t tests 18, 75, 77, 80, each now carrying this task in
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv.
subject: can residue in t/op/universal.t: a FORWARD-DECLARED sub is not can-able, a NUMBER as a class name is not, and an IO bareword invocant is not
